mapping_basis: Stotra Nidhi numbers exactly ten canonical stanzas 51-1 through 51-10 and provides a completion marker. Each numbered Facebook image is mapped to the stanza printed in its own #N caption. Caption prose was checked against that canonical stanza; all omitted or conflicting scene elements are documented individually and Sanskrit controls composition. Three nostanza images are unmapped because they are text or handwritten-note images and every canonical stanza already has a captioned picture.
source_photo_role: Attributed Facebook group story/context references only; not identity/style references, translations, or approval.

references.caption:
#1
One early morning, Krishna wished to go for a picnic to the forest along with the Gopas. They carried eatables, cooked rice and all delicacies and left to the forest with the cows.
references.observed_reference: Broadly aligned: Krishna and the cowherd group move among cattle in a forest pasture. The image does not clearly show the food carried for the outing or establish the early hour.
references.mapping_note: Use as broad departure/pasture context; canonical verse determines that Krishna leaves with Vraja children and many calves, carrying food.

references.caption:
#2
As Krishna walked through the forest, the sages collected the dust raised by Krishna's tiny lotus feet, smeared their body with it, which has power to purify the three worlds.
references.observed_reference: Mismatch by omission: Krishna walks through a herd and dust is visible, but no sages collecting or applying the dust appear.
references.mapping_note: Retain as Krishna/cattle context only; compose the canonical sages and dust action.

references.caption:
#3
As Krishna and Gopas were grazing the cows in the forest grasslands, suddenly the most terrifying Aghasura demon appeared in the form of a Python and blocked the way.
references.observed_reference: Broadly aligned but incomplete: a huge serpent lies across a green hill and small people/cattle appear at its base; Krishna is not distinct and the blocked path is not clear.
references.mapping_note: Use only as serpent scale and pastoral context; clearly show Krishna with the cowherd boys and cattle, and Aghasura blocking their route.

references.caption:
#4
When Krishna moved a little away, the Gopas mistook the huge body of the Asura as a mountain and its large spread out mouth as a cave. In their eagerness to explore the forest, they entered the python's open mouth.
references.observed_reference: Mismatch/incomplete: a snake-shaped cave dominates a green landscape; tiny figures are present, but the captioned gopa entry is not clearly legible. The source image includes the readable word “AGHASURA”.
references.mapping_note: Use only for the metaphor of a mountain-sized body and cave-like mouth; omit text and show gopas/cattle entering while Krishna remains at a distance.

references.caption:
#5
When the Gopas reached the snake's belly, they could not withstand the excessive heat and they cried for help. Krishna entered the snake’s mouth to save his helpless friends.
references.observed_reference: Caption/action mismatch: Krishna stands outside and gestures toward a giant open snake mouth, while the verse centers on the trapped, overheated herd and Krishna entering to rescue them.
references.mapping_note: Keep as serpent-mouth context only; depict the heat, helpless gopas and calves inside, with Krishna entering to save them.

references.caption:
#6
Krishna kept increasing his size at the throat of the python so much that Aghasura’s breath got choked and cried in pain. Krishna tore the snake's neck killing Aghasura. The Gopas and the cows were saved and came out from the python’s mouth.
references.observed_reference: Partial alignment: Krishna engages the giant snake mouth, but the throat constriction and the safe emergence of gopas and cattle are not clear.
references.mapping_note: Use as rescue context only; show Krishna expanded at the throat, the snake defeated without gore, and the herd emerging safely.

references.caption:
#7
Brilliant light radiated from the body of the snake reaching the sky and then emerged Krishna as Bhagwan came out of the huge snake. Brahma, other Gods and divine sages showered flowers on Krishna.
references.observed_reference: Clear mismatch: the picture shows a small seated Krishna beneath a coiled serpent hood, not the great light from Aghasura’s body merging into Krishna as gods dance and sing.
references.mapping_note: Do not copy the serpent-hood scene. Compose the celestial light and gods’ dance from the canonical verse; no beams or shafts.

references.caption:
#8
Then Krishna, Balarama and the Gopas enjoyed the lunch picnic by eating the delicious food. Brahma, Devas and other Gods were wonder struck at Krishna seeing the happenings in the forest.
references.observed_reference: Broadly aligned: Krishna shares a forest meal with a crowd. Brahma and the gods are not clearly identifiable, and several figures read as women rather than cowherd boys.
references.mapping_note: Use the picnic as broad meal context; caption #8 adds Balarama, whom the canonical stanza does not name, so omit him. Show Krishna, distinct cowherd boys, and astonished Brahma and gods following the return.

references.caption:
#9
Krishna holding a ball of rice in his hand entertained the Gopas with his humorous talks. Brahma and other Gods watched the above scene and sang joyfully in praise of Krishna.
references.observed_reference: Mismatch: Krishna is surrounded by women and repeated-looking Krishna figures; the ball of food, waist-tucked horn and flute, and humorous address to cowherd boys are not clearly shown.
references.mapping_note: Use only the meal setting; show one Krishna, a hand-held morsel, flute and horn at his waist, and distinct gopa boys laughing.

references.caption:
#10
The great Gods admired the love shown by Krishna, when He was enjoying the food with the Gopas more than He would have enjoyed the sacrificial yagnas offered by Gods and sang praises.
Bhattathiri prayed to Lord Guruvayoorappan to protect him from his ailments.

references.observed_reference: Partial scene match but central emphasis missing: Krishna eats among a crowd, but the source does not clearly distinguish gods praising him or compare the gopas’ meal with sacrificial offerings. Several surrounding figures read as women.
references.mapping_note: Keep only broad meal context; emphasize the gods’ praise and the canonical comparison with their sacrificial meals.
